concerns.quote: As matters stand, in a community pharmacy setting, there is no way of communicating clinical urgency between prescriber and pharmacy staff at the time the prescription is downloaded. A large number of prescriptions are downloaded every day by pharmacies. Urgent and non-urgent prescriptions look the same on the system. It is only at the labelling stage that any clinicians' comments can be seen.
concerns.hazard: lack of clinical urgency communication in community pharmacy prescription download system

concerns.quote: We were told that a different system (Vision) is used in scenarios where a pharmacy is run by a GP practice. This system is often used in rural settings. The Vision system allows for a prescription to be marked with a red exclamation mark at the point of downloading, where a prescription is urgent.
concerns.hazard: absence of red exclamation mark urgency indicator in NHS Spine prescriptions

concerns.quote: the investigation, an experienced clinical pharmacist who works at the GP practice attended the pharmacy and looked at the system in question. When 2 accessing the 'help section' of the software, the information she saw suggested that the red exclamation mark system was available and she questioned why this was not being used. It is not clear why this information is included in the 'help section' of software that does not currently support this function. It clearly led to confusion
concerns.hazard: misleading help documentation suggesting red exclamation mark functionality

concerns.quote: The GP issued a prescription to a nominated chemist, but a few minutes later put the system details back to what they were before the prescription was issued. Unbeknown to the GP these changes meant the prescription was no longer available for download by the chemist.
The results of the hospital urine test were available on the 20th April 2019 but were not acted upon at this point
The evidence was that had the patient received the medication prescribed by the GP or indicated by the hospital results, then she would not have died when she did

links.explanation: Both reports concern failures that prevent a prescription from being downloaded or accessed by the pharmacy. The earlier issue stems from a time‑limited download policy, while the later issue arises from a GP resetting the system after issuing the prescription.
